items.summary: On November 9, 2026, Cecilia Isola reported that the European Commission published preliminary findings stating TikTok failed to comply with the Digital Services Act by inadequately assessing and mitigating the “rabbit hole effect” of its For You feed recommender system. The Commission found non-compliance under Article 34 DSA for risk assessment and Article 35 DSA for mitigation, noting repeated recommendations may expose users to harmful content on mental health, sadness, isolation or body image. TikTok’s report assigns Medium-High severity and Likely probability overall but offers limited detail on sequences after initial viewing. In March 2025, 2,619,937 EU users had filtered keywords or hashtags, roughly 1.6% of the 159 million average monthly active users reported for July-December 2024 (p. 7). TikTok may now exercise its right to defense; if findings are confirmed, a fine could reach up to but not more than 6% of worldwide annual turnover.
items.title: EU Commission Finds TikTok Failed on Rabbit Hole Risk

items.summary:
At this week's Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, Texas, NVIDIA introduced open robotics technologies aimed at teaching robots delicate manipulation tasks like aligning gears and connecting cables. Among its announcements is GR00T 2, a world action model that completed 40 of 50 evaluated tasks without demonstrations and reached 95% success with five per task. AlphaNIST achieved more than 98% training success on the NIST Assembly Task Board using roughly 39x less GPU time. NVIDIA partnered with companies including Bosch Research, Siemens and UC Berkeley to demonstrate these tools at CoRL.

visual null
items.title: NVIDIA Unveils Simulation Tools for Dextrous Robot Tasks at CoRL

items.summary: NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for four of Korea's leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom, K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research, Solar Open 2 from Upstage, and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies. The recipes target NVIDIA B200 GPUs and are optimized for multi-node environments at data center scale. They claim to deliver up to 2x performance out of the box by handling request routing and communication across multiple GPUs.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Deployment Recipes for Korea's Leading Open Models

items.summary: Databricks is releasing Unity Catalog Dataset (UCDataset) in Beta on AI Runtime as a native PyTorch data loader that streams Unity Catalog tables directly to GPUs, eliminating exports and custom loading code. The article states the bottleneck in training runs is usually moving data to the chips rather than model performance. On simulated production workloads—streaming a 300 GB feature table across 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs—the company reports an average 10x improvement in training time versus reading from Parquet, though it frames this as self-reported benchmark results. UCDataset applies row filters and deletion vectors during reads and splits matching rows evenly across workers. It currently supports Delta tables only; plans to add multimodal support via the FILE type are noted.
items.title: Databricks Releases UCDataset for GPU Training

items.summary: Nvidia said it is investigating reports that its CEO Jensen Huang had a close relationship with Alice Huang, managing director of Singapore-based Megaspeed. The New York Times reported US officials suspect she worked for China's spy agency collecting intelligence. China denied the allegations as groundless and speculative. Nvidia stated it has no reason to believe its secrets were compromised but will examine all available information.
items.title: Nvidia Investigates Reports Linking CEO Jensen Huang to Alleged Chinese Spy Alice Huang

items.summary: Across the US, parents and teachers are criticizing Google's announcement that schools blocking AI tools could also lose access to Google Search. The company said it would keep Gemini products off K-12 student accounts until administrators turn them on explicitly. Chris Phillips, vice-president for education at Google, said they believe schools should control AI use in classrooms. Respondents raised concerns about weakened critical thinking and big tech influence, with some suggesting alternatives like DuckDuckGo or academic databases such as JSTOR.
items.title: Parents and Teachers Criticize Google's AI Block Search Threat

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, admitted to an affair in a message to employees obtained by the FT. The disclosure follows reports that US intelligence believed he had a relationship with Alice Huang, whom officials described as working for China's Ministry of State Security. Nvidia announced its board would launch an independent investigation into the foreign intelligence effort targeting him.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Affair Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: Jensen Huang began working with crisis communications firm Heller a year before admitting to an extramarital affair. Founded by Risa Heller, the firm has handled scandals for figures like Anthony Weiner and Mario Batali. Nvidia later instructed its teams to include Heller on press inquiries about Huang.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Hires Crisis PR Firm Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: Catalist-listed Food Innovators reported on Nov 9 that an employee may have misappropriated funds belonging to its wholly owned subsidiary F Innovators Singapore ($35,000) and two unidentified client companies ($324,000), totaling $359,000 as at Nov 9 based on preliminary investigations. The group said it has not named the employee or their position.
items.title: Food Innovators Suspects Worker Embezzled $359,000 from Unit and Clients

items.summary: IBM describes its open-source proxy server Praxis, which embeds the contributed Praxis Policy Engine (PPE) as a policy filter across ordinary and AI traffic. PPE treats tools, prompts, resources, model calls, and agents as explicit policy targets within a reference monitor using verified state outside the model's control. IBM-affiliated contributors hold maintainer roles, and Praxis has been onboarded into the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox.
items.title: IBM Contributes Policy Engine to Open-Source AI Proxy Praxis

items.summary: Elith and NVIDIA released Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan, a synthetic dataset extension of the open-source Nemotron-Personas-Japan collection. It pairs Japan's official demographic statistics with household finance and financial literacy data to support agentic AI development without using real customer information. The release holds 9M personas across 50 fields, roughly 50% more than its predecessor, under a CC BY 4.0 license allowing commercial use. Development drew on feedback from Sompo Japan, Tokio Marine Holdings, Bank of Fukuoka, Mizuho Financial Group, Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance and the Financial Data Utilization Association (FDUA). The dataset is designed for customer simulation, model evaluation and bias testing across Japanese society.
items.title: Elith and NVIDIA Release Synthetic Japanese Financial Persona Dataset

items.summary: Mixture‑of‑Experts models store every expert in memory even though most stay idle per token; for Qwen3.5‑122B, ~95% of its footprint is expert MLPs while only 8 experts are used per layer. The authors introduce HOPE (Higher‑Order Pruning of Experts), a second‑order pruning method that accounts for pairwise interactions between co‑activated experts rather than scoring them independently as first‑order methods do. At 50% pruning, HOPE achieves the best average rank across conditions and gains up to +6.1% on agentic coding tasks over REAP; at 50% its rank improves to 1.58 versus 2.42 for REAP. The authors evaluated it on three models with two calibration datasets against four baselines, noting the advantage grows at higher pruning rates and that cross‑layer interactions remain preliminary.
items.title: HOPE Prunes MoE Experts Using Pairwise Interactions

items.summary: In an essay dated Nov 9, 2026, Matthew Kirschenbaum argues that natural language has become a new attack surface for agentic systems. Drawing on the history of phone phreaking and injection attacks like SQL injection and prompt injection, he frames recent OpenAI and Hugging Face events as evidence that code and data now flow interchangeably across networks. He notes tens of thousands of lines of agent-shared text were analyzed by AI investigators, and cites Eryk Salvaggio's description of systems as a pinball machine for words. The piece distinguishes this from earlier cyberattacks like Stuxnet, emphasizing the widespread availability of agentic technology. Kirschenbaum warns that future models may absorb postmortems into their training mesh.
items.title: Language as Attack Surface in AI Era

items.summary: A Singaporean writer, Tham Kwok Keong, describes his 79-year-old father needing two blood tests on Nov 11 at Khatib Polyclinic and Khoo Teck Puat Hospital just 30 minutes apart. Though he asked for one combined test, both facilities rejected it because their systems could not confirm what the other was testing. He cites this as evidence that the Health Information Bill (HIB), passed in 2026 to improve coordinated care, still has a long way to go.
items.title: Father's Two Same-Day Blood Tests Blocked by System Gap

items.summary: A Sport Singapore forum member, Daryl Tan Yan Liang, proposed progressively installing shelters or weather canopies over outdoor ActiveSG sports courts such as tennis, pickleball and futsal venues. He argued that rising heat and frequent downpours reduce court usability during midday hours and disrupt booked sessions. A phased rollout starting with high-demand courts could test benefits before wider expansion.
items.title: Singapore forum proposes shelters over outdoor sports courts

items.summary: Google Cloud announced that GKE dynamic slicing is generally available, decoupling logical TPU slice formation from physical nodepool provisioning. The company states it reduces AI workload startup times by up to 5x and workload recovery by 4.5x compared with static per-slice nodepools. Two engineers, Kavitha Gowda and Wenzhe Li of Google Cloud, present the feature. It comes in two forms: super-slicing, which stitches TPU cubes via optical circuit switching into larger slices, and sub-slicing, which partitions a single cube for multiple isolated workloads. The offering is supported only under TPU All Capacity reservation mode across all available regions, with documentation provided for getting started.
items.title: Google Cloud rolls out dynamic TPU slicing on GKE for resilience and efficiency

items.summary:
The Philippine economy contracted for a fifth straight quarter in July-September, with GDP rising just 2.1%, below the Reuters forecast of 3% and its weakest pace in over five years. Weak household and government spending plus a 4.8% drop in farm output drove the slowdown. Economic Planning Secretary Arsenio Balisacan said reaching the lower end of the government’s 3.5%-to-4.5% target would require 6.3% growth in Q4, which he called challenging amid elevated inflation and a corruption scandal weighing on business confidence.

visual null},
items.title: Philippines Misses Its Own Growth Target as Q3 Slips

items.summary: Researchers at Queen's University Belfast examine whether true zero-trust architectures can govern autonomous agent systems, arguing that over-reliance on a single trusted layer creates significant cyber risk. They report an in-house experiment showing de-authentication attacks via agentic orchestration could occur as fast as 2 to 3 seconds, leaving little time to react or patch. The team identifies threats such as context recovery and zero-day attacks, and proposes guardrails including AI bills of materials, distributed ledger technology for traceability, and formal verification of trust. They note that utility under low-trust governance offers short-term benefits while the cost of system failure remains unexplored (s27-s34). The work is supported by forthcoming papers at ICOIN 2026 and other venues (s59-72).
items.title: QUB Researchers Warn of Trust Failures in Agentic AI

items.summary: Tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, the eighth city it has entered, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles. The item notes this is Tesla's largest day-one map and more than four times Waymo's local area, but flags that much of it may not be bookable: an independent check found only about 59% usable in Austin. Robotaxi Tracker logged no Tesla vehicles as of Monday morning. Koby Pierce tested six cities and found real service between 59% and 78% of advertised areas, with railroad crossings cited as a factor. The item concludes the honest read is 'up to 274 square miles,' closer in practice to 160 to 210 square miles with an unknown number of cars and the airport off-limits. Tesla runs about 666 driverless vehicles nationally versus Waymo's over 4,000.
items.title: Tesla Opens Robotaxi in San Antonio Amid Doubt Over Real Coverage

items.summary: The International Energy Agency is backing faster electrification as the climate summit opens in Antalya, Turkey. Its special report says cost-effective technologies could let electricity meet 33% of global final energy use by 2035, up from 23%, putting a proposed 35% target within reach. The IEA said current prices amid the Strait of Hormuz crisis would make more electrification affordable and cut fuel-importing nations' bills by over $400 billion combined by 2035, with faster adoption using about 18 million fewer barrels of oil daily.
items.title: IEA Supports Electrification Push at COP31 Climate Summit

items.summary: Allegations of corporate espionage tied to Nvidia, combined with rising political opposition to data center construction in the US, could reshape the superpower tech race. A Reuters columnist noted that while controversy over Nvidia's CEO may help Huawei, Beijing has more to lose if export controls tighten. Democratic midterm wins might slow AI rollout, giving China a window; an economist said China would see slowdowns as chances to catch up.
items.title: Nvidia Rivals See AI Race Opportunity Amid US Headwinds

items.summary: The EU filed a lawsuit against IBM, Atos and Leonardo over delays in delivering its entry/exit system (EES), revealed in the bloc’s IT agency EU-Lisa annual accounts. The system has faced significant difficulties since launching in October 2025, including three-hour waiting times at peak periods from outages and staffing shortages. EU-Lisa said a claim was submitted on 22 December 2025 to an Estonian court.
items.title: EU Sues Consortium Over Troubled Border System

items.summary: A Rail Accident Investigation Branch report says a train killed an Amazon delivery driver, Brandon Hatcher, who drove his van onto tracks at the Bax crossing near Teynham in July. Inspectors called it “an obvious risk of further tragedy” and urged Network Rail and the Department for Transport to overhaul this type of manually operated level crossing, where signs may have misled him into thinking he could enter with only the entry gate open. A second similar death is under investigation.
items.title: Rail inquiry flags danger at manual crossings after Amazon driver killed

items.summary: On Nov 9, Meta Platforms announced it would expand its AI age-estimation technology globally across Instagram, Facebook and Messenger to move more teens into Teen Account protections. Parents in the US will begin receiving notifications this month; Australia already uses Apple's age-range signal. The rollout comes as Meta faces multiple lawsuits alleging harm to young users, including an August settlement worth up to $18 billion with nearly every US state.
items.title: Meta Expands AI Age Checks for Instagram Teens Amid Lawsuits

items.summary: On November 9, Alphabet's Google introduced two new variations of its in-house tensor processing units: the 8tx and the 8i Max. The company said TPU sales contributed meaningfully to results in the September quarter, with Google Cloud revenue more than doubling to $30.71 billion. Alphabet shares rose more than 3 per cent in early trading as the launches step up its challenge to Nvidia's dominance in AI chips.
items.title: Google launches redesigned AI chips as cloud revenue doubles, pressuring Nvidia

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell around 4% to $178.44 on Monday after the AI chipmaker launched an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation, following his admission of an extramarital affair and reports linking him to Alice Huang of Megaspeed. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe secrets were compromised; China called the spy claims groundless. Huang will remain CEO during the review.
items.title: Nvidia Investigates Foreign Intel Probe After Huang Affair Admission

items.summary: Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese businesswoman with media, finance and technology experience who has become the focus of scrutiny over suspected links to China's intelligence establishment. Her association with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which buys Nvidia AI chips and leases computing capacity to Chinese firms, raises questions about whether an intelligence operation targeted the chipmaker. Reports also cite her relationship with Jensen Huang as adding to concern.
items.title: Alice Huang at Centre of Nvidia Controversy

items.summary: An article reports that Nvidia's internal investigation of its chief executive adds to a series of difficulties confronting the company, which is described as the world's most valuable chip firm. Among these pressures are large Democratic gains in midterm elections that could slow AI infrastructure spending in the United States, growing competition from Amazon and Google over custom chips, and rising funding for startup rivals seeking to challenge Nvidia.
items.title: Nvidia's CEO investigation joins mounting challenges for chipmaker

items.summary: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang after Bloomberg reported that a foreign intelligence effort targeted him amid allegations of an affair. Nvidia shares fell roughly 5% on Monday. The company said it has no reason to believe national security or trade secrets were compromised, and the inquiry will examine all available information.
items.title: Nvidia Board Investigates Jensen Huang After Alleged Spy Link and Personal Affair

items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 619 points, or 1.2%, in Monday trading as oil prices declined. West Texas Intermediate futures fell close to 3% near $88 a barrel while Brent lost over 3% around $95. Nvidia stock dropped 5% in premarket trading after its board launched a probe of CEO Jensen Huang amid spying suspicions, though he intends to stay.
items.title: Dow Climbs as Oil Slides and Nvidia Falls on Board Probe

items.summary: Barnichon and Mesters of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco summarize a paper that compares monetary policy across economic environments using estimated impulse responses rather than a structural model. Applying their framework to 150 years of history, they find meaningful improvements occurred only in the last thirty years, concentrated in better responses to financial shocks after Volcker and weaker reactions to supply-side disturbances during the Great Inflation. The authors caution that separating policy quality from economic circumstances is difficult because policymakers do not fully control the environment.
items.title: A 150-Year View Shows U.S. Monetary Policy Improved Only Recently

items.summary: Chernov, Kelly, Malamud and Schwab estimate the maximal Sharpe ratio achievable across large asset cross-sections without building an efficient portfolio. Their method yields tight bounds and finds U.S. equities reach about 7.4 (5.0 excluding micro-caps), far above existing benchmarks of 1.0–4.0, while corporate bonds add little significant gain.
items.title: Researchers Estimate Hidden Maximum Sharpe Ratio in Asset Portfolios

items.summary: Jin, Wagman and Xing study California's AB 537 law requiring fee-inclusive Airbnb prices from July 1, 2024. Using Coarsened Exact Matching of San Diego and San Francisco versus Seattle and Chicago listings, they find all-in pricing made guests more price-sensitive yet average daily rates rose by 4.8 percent.
items.title: California Short-Term Rental Fee Law Raised Prices Despite Transparency

items.summary: This FRED Blog post explains that the U. S. Census Bureau's Annual Integrated Economic Survey (AIES) is one of the building blocks of the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) industry accounts, and it connects to how each September the BEA revises GDP, GDP by industry, and state-level statistics in an annual update incorporating more complete source data; a graph compares AIES manufacturing shipments with BEA's quarterly gross output for manufacturing from the first quarter of 2007 through the second quarter of 2026.
items.title: How FRED's AIES Benchmarks Feed BEA Industry Output

items.summary: Germany pledged EUR 500,000 to the Global Trust Fund to strengthen trade capacity in developing economies and least developed countries. Ambassador Heidecke said Germany is glad to renew its commitment. The fund finances about 280 activities yearly; since establishment it supported over 2,800 workshops, training 19,000 participants in 2024 alone.
items.title: Germany Pledges Half a Million Euros to WTO Trade Fund

items.summary: Kashim Chowdhury, a civil servant from east London aged 56, has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud after the jury unanimously concluded he acted with deliberate and intentional dishonesty. Between 2020 and September 2023 he held eight full-time public sector roles that overlapped, earning £350,000 in total, including more than £284,000 from taxpayers' money during spring 2023 when five jobs coincided. He was contracted to work 183 hours a week and refused bail pending sentencing.
items.title: Civil servant jailed for secretly holding five overlapping public sector jobs

items.summary: Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, told BBC Panorama that affordability is her overriding objective as she seeks to reduce household bills while preserving public support for climate action. She argued that homegrown renewables and nuclear would decouple Britain from global fossil fuel markets and lower costs in the long term. However, she conceded that rising prices have put consensus on reducing carbon emissions under pressure, though she rejected blaming net zero for higher bills. The interview arrives as ministers face a predicted surge in energy prices in January, expected to be the biggest rise in four years, amid opposition attacks on subsidy schemes and debates over drilling at the Jackdaw gas field and Rosebank oil field.
items.title: Energy Secretary Prioritises Bill Cuts Amid Climate Pressure

items.summary: Nvidia placed its chief executive, Jensen Huang, under an independent investigation after reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort linked to his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing. Nvidia stock fell 5% in pre-market trading as a result. The company's board said it had no reason to believe US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but its inquiry would examine all available information. Republican lawmakers have asked Huang to brief the House foreign affairs and intelligence committees next week on Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage. This story is part of First Thing, a daily news briefing from The Guardian covering global headlines including climate talks in Turkey, US midterm fallout for Trump, and the death of a Kraków shooting suspect.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Under Independent Investigation Over Spy Claims; Stock Falls

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 6.4% on Monday, erasing roughly $325 billion from its market value at the opening of trading as shares reached about $174.70. The board launched an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation tied to Alice Huang of MegaSpeed. China called the allegations baseless speculation and a smear, while Nvidia stressed it had no reason to believe confidential information was compromised ahead of its Nov. 17 earnings report.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Drops After Board Investigates Intelligence Allegations Against Huang

items.summary: The European Union plans to name a successor to Christine Lagarde, who announced on October 29 that she is leaving the ECB prematurely after seven years. Eurogroup chief Kyriakos Pierrakakis said Monday the goal is completion by year-end, though he noted final selection rests with EU leaders rather than finance ministers. Candidates include Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernandez de Cos.
items.title: EU Targets Year-End Appointment for New ECB Chief

items.summary: A news page dated 09 November 2026 reports that Turkish President Erdogan met with Apple CEO Tim Cook, naming both leaders as the item's subjects. The page carries no figures, statements or direct quotes beyond this meeting report.
items.title: Turkish President Erdogan Meets Apple CEO Tim Cook

items.summary: Spain's Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo has endorsed former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos as a candidate to replace Christine Lagarde at the European Central Bank. Speaking to Euronews, Cuerpo cited Hernández de Cos's economic expertise and reputation as a consensus-builder. Madrid is competing with the Netherlands' Klaas Knot for the role. Lagarde intends to step down on 7 February next year.
items.title: Spanish minister backs Hernández de Cos for ECB presidency

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, came under public attention on Monday after acknowledging an extramarital relationship with a woman that US officials say worked for Chinese intelligence. Beijing denied the allegation.
items.title: Nvidia chief Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over affair and espionage claims

items.summary: Alice Huang (Huang Le), a Chinese businesswoman with little publicly known background, is at the centre of an alleged intelligence operation targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. US intelligence agencies believe she was recruited by Beijing to gather information on him. The two share a surname but are not related. Photographs from 2024 and footage from a May 2025 dinner in Taipei show them together, though these appear to be evidence rather than proof of the alleged operation.
items.title: Alice Huang, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and an alleged Beijing spy link

items.summary: Twenty-five young representatives from BRICS countries gathered in Fuzhou, southeast China's Fujian Province, for the six-day 2026 BRICS Youth Leaders Campus on Science, Technology and Innovation, running November 8 to 13. The camp is organized by the All-China Youth Federation and hosted by the China International Youth Exchange Center under the theme 'Bringing Together Youth Innovation to Advance Practical BRICS Cooperation.' Wang Tingting, head of the International Projects Department at the center, told CGTN that the program aims to translate exchanges into practical cooperation for young innovators.
items.title: BRICS Youth Leaders Campus Opens in Fuzhou

items.summary: The 31st session of the UN climate conference opens Monday in Antalya, Türkiye, focusing on turning national pledges into emissions cuts. A UNFCCC synthesis report found current commitments would reduce emissions by only about 6% by 2035 versus around 9% if fully implemented against 2019 levels. Adaptation finance also lags: UNEP estimates developing countries need $305 billion annually, while public flows reached just $28.2 billion to $31.7 billion in 2024, covering only 20 to 29% of needs even if tripled by 2035.
items.title: COP31 in Türkiye Tests Climate Pledges and Finance

items.summary: Teddy Riner, France's five-times Olympic gold medallist and judo star aged 37, has announced plans to run in next year's presidential election. Describing himself as neither leftwing nor rightwing, he said his aim is to
items.title: Judo Champion Teddy Riner Enters French Presidential Race

items.summary: Li Rui of Fudan University argues the ninth China International Import Expo shows that openness is 'not an either-or choice.' The expo drew 162 countries and a record 4,142 overseas exhibitors across more than 440,000 square meters. American firms occupied over 50,000 square meters for eight straight years, yet free booth space for least developed countries rose 17% this year while the zone for African products was upgraded under China's zero tariffs. The author cites a Rwandan exhibitor who grew from chili samples to shipping 300 tons by container in 2025 as evidence that small booths can lead to lasting trade.
items.title: CGTN analyst frames CIIE as inclusive openness, not rich-only club

items.summary:
On Monday, November 9, 2026, China launched the 29th group of satellites for its low-Earth-orbit satellite internet constellation from the Hainan commercial space launch site in Wenchang. A Long March-12 rocket blasted off at 4:24 a.m., placing the satellites into their preset orbit. Officials said this was the country's first single-core, 4-meter-class rocket and marked the 676th flight of the Long March series.

visual null},
items.title: China Launches 29th Group of LEO Internet Satellites on Long March-12

items.summary: The Communist Party of China has launched the process to elect delegates to its 21st national congress, scheduled for the second half of 2027 in Beijing. An official from the Organization Department explained that the election matters because a new central committee and discipline inspection body will be chosen. The 2,360 delegates should represent more than 101 million members.
items.title: China Begins Selecting Delegates for 21st Party Congress in 2027

items.summary: Thick smog enveloped New Delhi on Monday, with the air quality index surpassing 350 and entering the severe category. Although courts had restricted conventional firecrackers in favor of green alternatives during Diwali, residents still set off fireworks that released particulate matter into the atmosphere. Residents reported throat irritation and eye itching, while experts called government measures knee-jerk and temporary.
items.title: Smog Blankets New Delhi as Diwali Firecrackers Fuel Pollution Crisis

items.summary: British comedian Russell Brand was jailed for more than 10 years on Monday for a string of sex offences including rape. The judge told him he had been a 'sexual predator' whose fame had protected him.
items.title: Russell Brand Sentenced To Over Ten Years For Rape And Assault

items.summary: At least 39 people died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal heading toward Spain's Canary Islands, the Senegalese Press Agency reports. One survivor was rescued and nationalities remain unconfirmed as searches continue along a 25km (15-mile) stretch complicated by strong currents. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye offered condolences and pledged to dismantle smuggling networks amid renewed concerns over dangerous sea crossings.
items.title: Senegal Boat Sinking Kills at Least 39 Migrants

items.summary: British comedian Russell Brand was sentenced to over ten years in prison after being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Judge Justice Bennathan set the total sentence at 10 years, six months during proceedings at Southwark Crown Court in London on Monday. A jury had earlier convicted him last week on four of seven counts, including raping a woman he met at a show in 2009 and sexually assaulting three women between 2004 and 2009. Brand denies all charges and said he never had non-consensual sex. The prosecution called for a long sentence citing aggravating circumstances; the defence argued he was "a fundamentally different person" from who he was at the time of the crimes.
items.title: Russell Brand Sentenced To Over Ten Years For Rape And Sexual Assault

items.summary:
Misinformation threatens democracy across Africa, especially before elections, as artificial intelligence makes it easier to manipulate images, voices and videos. Dani Madrid-Morales of the University of Sheffield told DW that few countries do a good job combating fake news, while civil society groups like Africa Check fill gaps left by governments. An Afrobarometer study found over 60% view China's influence positively versus 52% for the United States and only 34% for France. Initiatives such as Ghana's Caravan of Hope reached 3,000 people in five districts. Madrid-Morales warns some programs breed distrust, while governments elsewhere use laws to silence dissent rather than fight disinformation genuinely.

visual:null},
items.title: African Nations Grapple With Disinformation and Media Literacy

items.summary: Three weeks before Spain's general election, polls show the conservative People's Party trailing Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's Socialists but still ahead. The PP would need to ally with far-right Vox for a parliamentary majority; SocioMetrica projects around 200 seats combined for them versus 108 for the Socialists. A separate 40dB survey puts the gap at two points, while Sigma Dos sees Sanchez winning 105 seats against 199 for PP and Vox. Sanchez called the snap election on October 5 after right-wing parties blocked housing legislation.
items.title: Spanish Right Holds Poll Lead Over Sanchez's Socialists Before November Election

items.summary: A CGTN opinion column argues that clean energy is reshaping rural development in China, turning green growth into tangible benefits for people. It points to Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, where wind power revenues have become a stable source of collective income for 132 villages, and notes similar effects elsewhere: Shandong Province converts sunshine into electricity supporting local industries, while Henan helps businesses cut costs so more development gains reach villagers.
items.title: China's Clean Energy Brings Growth to Rural Villages

items.summary: US stocks rose sharply, with the Dow Jones gaining 569.51 points and the Nasdaq Composite up 2.53% to 24,931.00. Chip stocks rebounded after last week’s selloff, though an internal Nvidia investigation into possible foreign intelligence targeting of Jensen Huang raised concerns about its leadership. Analysts at Morgan Stanley and UBS called the rout overdone, while El Bilassy warned focus on Nvidia may ease as inflation data approaches.
items.title: US Stocks Rally as Nvidia Probe Weighs on Tech

items.summary: Google is introducing two new variations of its tensor processing units, or TPUs, as it broadens its lineup of artificial intelligence chips in a push against Nvidia. The latest versions will support confidential computing and longer context windows for tasks such as drug discovery and coding. Alphabet shares rose up to 3.2% on the news. Google's TPU sales are estimated at $12 billion this year, with projected growth past $135 billion by 2028. The chips pair with AMD processors and compete in a market dominated by Nvidia GPUs, though TPUs cost about 30% less.
items.title: Google Unveils Specialized AI Chips to Challenge Nvidia

items.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party leader Rajeev Chandrasekhar mocked China after the country rejected allegations of spying on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the claims baseless. He said China relies on honeytrapping to access technology cheaply and faster than through research. The denial coincides with an independent investigation into whether a foreign intelligence operation involving Alice Huang targeted Mr Huang.
items.title: BJP leader mocks China's espionage claims over Nvidia chief

items.summary: Nvidia Corp. has opened an independent investigation into its Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after reports that his romantic relationship with a woman tied to Megaspeed International could involve foreign intelligence activity. The disclosure sent Nvidia shares down about 5% in premarket trading, implying roughly $225 billion of market capitalisation loss. A board committee is working with outside counsel while the CEO said he supports and will cooperate fully with the inquiry. Analyst Stacy Rasgon flagged a key man risk given Huang’s central role, and President Donald Trump defended him as a fine person who should remain CEO. The company stated it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised but promised to examine all available information.
items.title: Nvidia Launches Probe Into Jensen Huang Over Alleged Spy Affair

items.summary: Reuters could not determine where former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang is or independently verify her employment, after US authorities reportedly concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by foreign intelligence. Republican lawmakers requested a briefing on the allegations and company security procedures; Nvidia said its Asian cloud customers receive ordinary business information.
items.title: Nvidia Spy Probe Deepens as Alice Huang's Location Remains Unclear

items.summary: On Monday, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs dismissed claims that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was part of a spy plot as an unsubstantiated smear campaign against Beijing. According to The New York Times, Huang admitted being intimate with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence linked to information gathering for China. He did not name her. Nvidia announced it would investigate the matter.
items.title: China Rejects Spy Allegations Against Jensen Huang

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell over 8% in Monday's opening trade after the company announced a board-level investigation into whether chief executive Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The inquiry follows reports linking him to Alice Huang, whom US authorities concluded was an asset of Chinese intelligence. Bernstein expects demand for Nvidia products to hold but warns of regulatory risks and calls it potentially distracting; Nadia El Bilassy at Equiti Group said the move added pressure on AI-linked stocks as investors pull out.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Falls After Intelligence Probe Into CEO

items.summary: Meta said Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation technology globally, moving millions more Instagram users into Teen Account protections even when their birth dates show adulthood. The move comes as Meta faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young people and after $18 billion settlements with US states over teen harm. Teen Accounts limit who can contact teens, the content they see and their time on apps. (Source: Reuters)
items.title: Meta Broadens AI Age Checks Globally Amid Teen-Harm Lawsuits

items.summary: An evening newswrap leads with US intelligence suspecting a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang (Huang Le), of espionage tied to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. It then covers Delhi's AQI turning 'severe' after Diwali, several areas crossing 400; Iran's leaked letter detailing oil terminals in China; Sheikh Hasina seeking a fresh passport and NID before her December return; and Rahul Gandhi challenging Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks. The piece is by Aryan Singh of The Times of India.
items.title: Nvidia boss implicated in Chinese spy scandal as Delhi hits severe air quality

items.summary: Singapore-based AI infrastructure company Megaspeed reaffirmed its denial of allegations that it illegally transferred Nvidia chips to China, standing by a December 23 statement rejecting the claims as misleading. Renewed scrutiny follows reports linking executive Alice Huang to Beijing and an admitted affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Megaspeed cited on-site inspections by US, Malaysian and Nvidia authorities, signalled possible legal action against Bloomberg, while sources say China dismissed the allegations.
items.title: Megaspeed denies chip-smuggling claims amid Jensen Huang affair probe

items.summary: On Monday, China dismissed allegations of a spy plot involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling them baseless and accusing critics of smearing Beijing. The claims followed a New York Times report that Huang told the board about an intimate relationship with someone US intelligence linked to information gathering for Beijing. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the allegation "nothing but smears against China." Nvidia launched its own investigation, and shares fell around 5% in pre-market trading.
items.title: China Rejects Spy Plot Claims Against Nvidia's Jensen Huang as Smears

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, acknowledged an extramarital relationship and apologized for hurting his wife Lori Mills and their children. The admission follows a media report linking him to a Chinese businesswoman suspected of sharing information with Beijing, prompting an internal investigation into possible foreign intelligence involvement. Huang accepted full responsibility in a letter to staff.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Infidelity in Letter to Employees

items.summary: New data show leatherback turtles nested in Galathea Bay, Great Nicobar Island, in record numbers last winter: 869 nests. That is the highest number of leatherback nests recorded on any beach in the Indian Ocean this season, ending in March. Experts say it underlines the need to protect the population, which has comparatively high genetic diversity and may be thriving. But no new genetic research has been conducted since 2001, likely because of a plan by the Indian government to build a transshipment terminal at Galathea Bay that could make the beach inaccessible. A researcher who wished to remain anonymous called it 'the million-dollar question.' The article notes information about Great Nicobar wildlife is often obtained only through Right to Information requests.
items.title: Galathea Bay's record nesting threatens a unique genetic stronghold
